title: RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0 - Tips I Wish I Knew Before Starting
author: ComfyQuesting
chapters: Dont rush to the new area
description:
Starting RuneScape: Dragonwilds for the first time at 1.0? Here are the beginner tips I wish I knew before jumping in!

00:00 Intro
00:50 Ignore old health guides
01:39 Fishing is useful
02:23 Skills are important
03:14 Movement has improved
04:00 Hotwheel and quickcast
04:40 Your base isnt just decoration
05:31 Dont rush to the new area
06:20 Dont throw away good weapons
06:58 Solo play and co op
07:49 This is only the beginning 



Let me know what platform you’re playing on and whether you’re jumping in solo or with friends!

#RuneScapeDragonwilds #Dragonwilds #RuneScape #BeginnerGuide #SurvivalGames #cozygames 

Join the discord! https://discord.gg/SWMDX2HKe

transcript.text: So RuneScape Dragon Wilds is finally leaving early access. And if you're one of the people planning to jump in for
the first time at launch, there's quite a lot going on. You've got survival, building, farming, fishing, magic,
dragons, a frankly unreasonable number of skills for me to get distracted by. And because Dragon Wilds has already
spent over a year changing during early access, there's quite a bit of advice floating around that just isn't true
anymore. So today I'm going through 10 things I think are genuinely worth knowing before you start RuneScape
Dragon Wilds at 1.0. And I've specifically based these on the newest version of the game and the
changes confirmed for launch, because I do not want to confidently send you off looking for a mechanic that was deleted
6 months ago. That would be embarrassing. So starting with probably the most important change for completely
new players, number one, ignore old health guides cuz the entire system changed. And if you've already been
watching old Dragon Wild guides, this is probably the biggest thing I want you to know. The health system has been
completely reworked. Ward stones and ward shields are gone. Instead, you increase maximum health by finding
constitution shrines around Ashen Fall. And rather than relying on health potions the way older versions of the
game did, food now directly restores your health. Healing potions were removed while stat potions stayed, which
means if you see an older guide telling you to build around ward shield or stat power healing potions, don't. It was
probably completely correct when they made the video, but now it's history. And personally, I actually like this
system a lot more because it makes exploring useful for something other than me finding a nice hill and
immediately deciding, yep, my house goes here. If you find constitution shrines while exploring, you're directly making
your character tougher. So definitely keep an eye out for them. Number two is fishing is way more useful than it
looks. And this follows directly from the health change, because normally in survival games, I see fishing and think,
cute, peaceful. I'll do that for 4 hours instead of progressing the story, which is probably still going to happen. But
in Dragon Wilds, fishing now has a really important practical use, too. Jagex specifically redesigned food so
that fish are the best in class option when it comes to pure health restoration, while other foods can offer
additional buffs. So, fishing isn't just a little side activity for people like me who enjoy standing next to the
digital ponds. It directly supports combat. The current fishing progression starts by crafting a fishing net and
speaking to the wise old man, and as you level the skill, you unlock things like rods and actual fishing skill spells.
So, I would start working on it much earlier than I normally would in a survival game. Number three, do not
treat skills like background XP. And this is probably one of the biggest differences between Jag and Wild and a
lot of other survival games because your skills aren't just number goes up, tree dies slightly faster. Leveling skills
can unlock proper abilities, passives, and magical skill spells. And one of the newest examples is agility. Agility was
added in the final major pre-launch update and it can eventually improve your stamina and carrying [music]
ability, as well as unlock things like an aerial dash, a second jump, and recall, which lets you place a marker
and teleport back to it. That means leveling isn't just about being more efficient. It can literally change how
you move around the world. And considering I have an incredible talent for seeing somewhere I'm very obviously
not supposed to reach it and thinking, "I can make that jump." Agility is probably going to save me from myself
quite a lot. There are six agility courses around Ashdale Forest, so if you find one while exploring, I really
wouldn't just ignore it. Number four is movement because it is much better than it used to be. And this is another
reason I'd be careful judging the launch version from really old gameplay because movement has had a lot of work. In the
newest pre-launch update, jumping was reduced from 20 stamina to 10. Agility can reduce that further, and jumps
gained more forgiveness around ledges. And Jagex has been improving networking behavior, so jumping works more
consistently in multiplayer. They've also added mounts over the course of early access. You can eventually get
things like the terrorbird, and later there's even a magic carpet design for traveling through the Umbral Sands. So,
I definitely won't spend the first few hours looking at every enormous distance on the map thinking, "Oh god, I'm
walking this whole place." Your movement options get significantly better. Just maybe don't expect the magic carpet 5
minutes after waking up, unfortunately. Number five is set up your hot wheel and quick cast early. This one's a lot less
exciting, but I genuinely think it'll make the game feel nicer almost immediately. The latest version added a
radial hot wheel for both controller and keyboard and mouse, and you can now assign a quick cast shortcut to either a
spell or an item. You can also cycle through your runes and arrows during combat instead of stopping to rummage
around your inventory, which sounds like a tiny quality of life change until you're being hit in the face by
something enormous while screaming, "Wait, they're the wrong arrows." So, before you get too far into the game,
actually spend a minute arranging your important items and deciding what you want on quick cast. Future panicking you
will appreciate this. Number six is your base is not just decoration, and this may be the tip I personally struggle
with the most because when a game gives me a building system, my priorities immediately become cute kitchen, cute
bedroom plants, and just save the world later. But Dragon Wilds actually integrates your base into progression.
Farming is a full skill, and Jagex designed it to work from the early areas of the game rather than only just being
something you discover near the end. You've got farming plots, composting, watering, plant diseases, tree growing,
and eventually skill spells like uproot and humidify. So, I wouldn't ignore base systems because you're desperate to
explore. Get yourself functional first, storage, crafting, food, farming, all the sensible survival things, then we
can spend 3 hours deciding which wall looks prettier because that's going to be the reward. And number seven is don't
assume the big new 1.0 area is where you should go first because one of the big reasons people are talking about Dragon
Wilds again is the new Scorned Wildness content coming with full release. But if
you're brand new, this is absolutely not where your journey starts. Scorned Wildness is the culmination of the
Koldra saga and contains the final confrontation with Queen Koldra. Jagex describes it as a raid style high-end
challenge with powerful enemies and end-game rewards including a dragon equipment. The broader progression takes
you through Ashdale's existing regions first including places like Brinewold, Fell Hollow, Dalden Reach, and the
Umbral Sands as the story builds towards Koldra. So, if you're watching the launch coverage and seeing reunite
dragon armor, 500 goddy, uh please don't assume you're supposed to have all of that by Tuesday afternoon. You're not
behind, you're just level four. It's okay. Number eight is don't throw away good weapons just because you've reached
a new tier. This is a newer progression change that's really worth knowing. The final
pre-launch update added ascension cores to the mystic forge. Those can be used to upgrade masterwork and vestige
weapons to higher tiers. So, if you get a weapon you really like, don't automatically assume, well, I will not
better materials now, goodbye forever. Some of those special weapons can continue progressing with you, which I
really like because I am kind of the person who gets emotionally attached to the weapon and refuses to replace it
because this one has been with me since Monday. Number nine, you can play alone but launch makes co-op much easier. You
do not need a Runescape group, a Discord clan, or 17 childhood friends to play this. Dragon Isles is designed to work
solo. But, if you do want to play with people, the 1.0 launch is a pretty huge improvement because it arrives
simultaneously across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S, and Nintendo Switch [music] too with cross-play confirmed.
The standard adventure supports you and up to three friends, and PC players also currently have dedicated server tooling
that can support larger groups. And if you're on Xbox, the game is also joining Game Pass on September the 15th. So, if
If been interested in Dragon Isles but couldn't convince your friends to buy another survival game, this might be
your moment. Begin the peer pressure. And finally, number 10, 1.0 is the end of Coelus' story, not the end of Dragon
Wilds. 1.0 is finishing the Coelus saga. It isn't Jagex saying, "Right, game finished. Time to go home." They've
already confirmed Dragon Wilds will continue receiving updates after launch with more skills, quests, regions,
bosses, enemies, and rewards planned. Jagex has also said updates will continue monthly with the next larger
update currently called Luminance planned for winter. And despite leaving early access, the standard game's price
is staying at $24.99 or $30 rather than increasing at 1.0. So, the September release is really the complete first
saga, the proper console launch, and the beginning of whatever Dragon Wilds becomes next, which is honestly probably
the thing that makes me most interested in jumping in now cuz there's already a lot here. So, those are the 10 things I
think are actually worth knowing before starting RuneScape Dragon Wilds at 1.0. And the biggest thing I'd keep in mind
is just how much this game has changed during early access. So, if you're watching the older guides, definitely
check when they're uploaded before you're building your entire character around something that may not even exist
anymore. Personally, I'm already very excited about the combination of exploring, building, farming, and
leveling skills. Although, I do have a horrible feeling I'm probably going to just spend my whole time decorating. If
you're planning to play Dragon Wilds at launch, let me know what you're playing on and whether you're jumping in solo or
with friends. And if this helped, feel free to leave a like and subscribe for more cozy games guides and probably me
getting distracted by farming systems I absolutely wasn't supposed to spend 6 hours on. Thank you so much for watching
and I'll see you in the next one. Bye.
